Subject: Hosted API SLOs — clarification and transient degradation carveout request

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers and burst handling looked promising. Before we move the pilot to production, our infrastructure and compliance teams need explicit language around measurement windows for p50/p95 and a potential carveout for nightly batch spikes that cause short-duration tail latency degradations.

Specifically we ask:
- Can Redwood commit to p50/p95 targets measured using a rolling 24-hour window or do you use fixed calendar windows?
- For predictable nightly batch jobs that temporarily increase queuing and tail latency for up to 45 minutes, can we have a transient-degradation exemption (up to X minutes per day) rather than counting the whole window against SLA?

I've attached an annotated request from our SREs to make the ask concrete (attachment: zephyrus_slo_request_annotated.pdf). We're aiming to sign the pilot addendum by the end of October if we can align on measurement language.

Best,
Alex Barton
Head of Platform Engineering
Zephyrus Health

Alex — thanks for the clear write-up and the annotated PDF. I looped in Karthik and Marissa so we can provide a combined technical and commercial response.

High level response: we can be flexible on the measurement window and provide a controlled carveout for short, scheduled degradations, but the language needs to be precise so it doesn't become an unbounded exception.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical measurement proposal (attached): our standard approach is a rolling 1-hour bucket aggregated into a 24-hour rolling window for reporting p50/p95. I've attached a spreadsheet that shows the reporting cadence and example calculations. (attachment: hosted-measurement-proposal-v3.xlsx)
2) Carveout proposal: allow up to two transient-degradation events per day, each up to 45 minutes, explicitly scheduled or pre-notified, subject to a monthly cap of N minutes.
3) Contract addendum: draft SLO addendum language for legal to review — Marissa will start with redlines.

Can you confirm: a) whether the nightly batch pattern is predictable (time window), and b) whether Zephyrus will accept a pre-notification requirement for scheduled windows? Once we have that I'll circulate a single-page SLO addendum for signature.

Naomi / Marissa — quick technical notes from infra side to support the proposal.

Summary: Redwood measures p50/p95 over rolling one-hour buckets that are then aggregated into a 24-hour rolling percentile. We prefer rolling windows because fixed calendar windows can mask short outages. That said, we can produce both a rolling and fixed view if the customer needs the fixed-window language in contract.

Carveout mechanics we recommend:
- Definition: transient-degradation event = any period where server-side queuing causes median latency > baseline by > 2x AND p95 breaches target for at least 5 continuous minutes.
- Allowed: up to two events/day, each capped at 45 minutes. Any leftover minutes in a month do not carry over.
- Telemetry requirement: customer must provide expected batch start/stop times at least 24 hours in advance OR mark events as scheduled via our partner API so we can tag traces and exclude them from SLA calculations.

Implementation details: we will add a metadata tag (zephyrus.scheduled_batch=true) and strip those requests from the SLO pipeline once verified. We will need a signed addendum and an SRE contact for incident correlation.

Attachment: runtime-metrics-spec.md (plain text) — contains the tag scheme and sample query.

karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — I reviewed the technical proposal. From a contracts perspective we can grant a tightly scoped transient-degradation exemption with these constraints:

- Exemption applies only to scheduled batch events that are both pre-notified 24 hours in advance and tagged via the partner API.
- Maximum exposure: 90 minutes/day total (two events, each <=45 minutes) and 1,800 minutes/month aggregate cap.
- Remedy when exceeded: events beyond the cap count toward breach calculations and are subject to our standard credit policy.
- Pricing: if the customer requests an expanded exemption (more minutes/day or no pre-notice), we will require a 10% uplift on committed usage pricing to offset scheduling risk.

I've attached a first-pass redline for the SLO addendum (slo-addendum-redline.docx). If Naomi gets a confirmation from Zephyrus that they accept the pre-notification and tagging requirement, I'll prepare a final clean addendum and route to legal and contracts for signature.

Marissa Cole

2) If you prefer tagging instead of pre-notice, provide a technical contact to arrange API access.
